newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Crude leads naphtha hike.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Crude leads naphtha hike.

text.p: Singapore naphtha rose on Wednesday after a big increase to overnight crude values supported by strong regional fundamentals where supplies are tight, traders said.
They said overnight August Brent gained 57 cents in London and had lost a mere three cents on Wednesday in London to last trade at $18.36.
The naphtha swaps rose sharply with August last quoted at $21.70/$21.80 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $21.25/$21.35, brokers said.
August swaps traded late Wednesday at $21.70 compared to Tuesday's $21.30 traded level.
The August/September spread has widened to value at 20 cents from 10 cents on Tuesday due to the prompt squeeze, they said.
Regional demand is strong due to the high operating rates of ethylene and aromatics plant.

In Singapore, the new 515,000 tonnes per year (tpy) ethylene plant which started up in late April is operating at its 100 percent capacity despite initial plans to operate at between 70 and 80 percent due to the late startup of downstream plants.
On top of this, aromatics producers in South Korea and Thailand have entered the market to purchase incremental naphtha supplies, traders said.
Regional supply is tight due to the reduction in refining output in Singapore on poor margins and the shutdown of one crude unit at Balikpapan for maintenance in July.
Traders said premiums for spot cargoes in Singapore have risen to above $1.00 per barrel after trading at this level late last week.
The gasoline market edged up on the crude jump with regional demand seen lacklustre.
A major was bidding for a 50,000-barrel cargo of 97-octane gasoline at $24.15 with another major offering a similar cargo at $24.20.
The 97/95-octane differential was valued at about $1.00 per barrel.
Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp has issued its first spot tender in about two years to import unleaded gasoline for delivery in August, a company official said on Wednesday.
The tender seeks 70,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline for August 11-15 delivery, on a cost-and-freight basis to Bataan.
The tender closes on July 18 and is vaild for the day. Industry sources said the import tender was issued due to high domestic demand and the shutdown of the thermal cracker.
